definitions.explanation: A mid-altitude cloud type made up of white or gray patches and rolls, often arranged in regular groups. Popularly called ひつじ{雲|ぐも} (sheep clouds) for their woolly appearance.

examples.japanese: {空|そら}に{高積雲|こうせきうん}が{広|ひろ}がる。
examples.english: Altocumulus clouds spread across the sky.

examples.japanese: {高積雲|こうせきうん}が{出|で}ると{天気|てんき}が{崩|くず}れやすい。
examples.english: When altocumulus clouds appear, the weather tends to turn.

examples.japanese: {夕方|ゆうがた}、{羊|ひつじ}の{群|む}れのような{高積雲|こうせきうん}が{茜色|あかねいろ}に{染|そ}まった。
examples.english: In the evening, altocumulus clouds like a flock of sheep were dyed crimson.

notes:
A mid-level cloud (the {積雲|せきうん} "cumulus" family at {高|こう} "high" altitude) made of small white or gray masses. Their appearance is often read as a sign of changing weather.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高積雲|こうせきうん}が{出|で}る: altocumulus clouds appear
- ひつじ{雲|ぐも}: sheep clouds — the everyday nickname for {高積雲|こうせきうん}

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {積乱雲|せきらんうん}: cumulonimbus — towering thunderclouds
- {巻積雲|けんせきうん}: cirrocumulus — similar ripples but much higher and finer
